The fix is correct. Let me trace through all the test cases to verify:

1. `wrap("the quick brown fox", 10)`: "the" (3) + " " + "quick" (5) = 9 ≤ 10 → "the quick"; then "brown" (5) + " " + "fox" (3) = 9 ≤ 10 → "brown fox". Result: `["the quick", "brown fox"]` ✓
2. `wrap("aaa bbb", 7)`: 3 + 1 + 3 = 7 ≤ 7 → stays on one line. Result: `["aaa bbb"]` ✓
3. `wrap("aaa bbb ccc", 7)`: "aaa bbb" fills exactly 7, then "ccc" (7+1+3=11 > 7) starts a new line. Result: `["aaa bbb", "ccc"]` ✓
4. `wrap("abcdefghij", 4)`: overlong word split into "abcd", "efgh", "ij" — unaffected by the change. Result: `["abcd", "efgh", "ij"]` ✓

The one-character-short bug was caused by the strict `<` comparison on line 32, which rejected lines that would be exactly `width` characters long. Changing it to `<=` matches the documented behavior ("a line may be exactly `width` long").
